"""Cohezion API - FastAPI server exposing swarm and MCP tools.

Thin entry point: creates the app, registers routes from
``routes_legacy``, and re-exports singletons for backward
compatibility (tests/conftest.py resets them via
``cohezion.api._vae_trainer = None``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, RedirectResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from cohezion.security.rate_limiter import get_rate_limiter

# Re-export singletons so ``cohezion.api._vae_trainer`` still works.
from .singletons import (  # noqa: F401
    _compute_coherence,
    _get_rl_policy,
    _get_vae,
    _rl_policy,
    _vae_trainer,
    set_token_client,
)


logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_CORS_ORIGINS = os.environ.get(
    "COHEZION_CORS_ORIGINS",
    "http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:8080",
).split(",")

app = FastAPI(
    title="Cohezion API",
    description="AI Research Lab API - Swarm workflows and MCP tools",
    version="0.1.0",
    docs_url="/docs" if os.environ.get("COHEZION_ENV") != "production" else None,
    redoc_url="/redoc" if os.environ.get("COHEZION_ENV") != "production" else None,
)

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=_CORS_ORIGINS,
    allow_credentials=False,
    allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
    allow_headers=["Content-Type", "Authorization", "X-Agent-Token"],
)


@app.middleware("http")
async def rate_limit_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    limiter = get_rate_limiter()
    client_ip = request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"
    result = limiter.check(client_ip, request.url.path)
    if not result.allowed:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=429,
            headers={
                "Retry-After": str(int(result.reset_after) + 1),
                "X-RateLimit-Limit": str(result.limit),
                "X-RateLimit-Remaining": "0",
            },
            content={"detail": "Rate limit exceeded"},
        )
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-RateLimit-Remaining"] = str(result.remaining)
    return response


static_dir = Path(__file__).parent / "static"
if static_dir.exists():
    app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=static_dir, html=True), name="static")


@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return RedirectResponse(url="/static/index.html")


def _register_routes() -> None:
    """Bind all route handlers from routes_legacy onto the app.

    This avoids duplicating route definitions here. The handlers
    in ``routes_legacy`` are plain async functions; this function
    attaches them to the FastAPI ``app`` with the correct HTTP
    method and path.
    """
    from . import routes_legacy as h
    from .models import (
        CompoundExecuteResponse,
        CompoundFeedbackResponse,
        CompoundHealthResponse,
        CompoundHistoryResponse,
        CompoundMetricsResponse,
        DebateResponse,
        FlumeDecodeResponse,
        FlumeEncodeResponse,
        FlumeInterpolateResponse,
        FlumeStatusResponse,
        FlumeTrainResponse,
        KnowledgeQueryResponse,
        PipelineStatusResponse,
        RlEpisodeResponse,
        RlPolicyInfoResponse,
        RLPolicyResponse,
        RlStepResponse,
        RLTrainResponse,
        SkillExecuteResponse,
        SwarmExecuteResponse,
        SystemMetricsResponse,
        TemplateParseResponse,
        TokenMetricsResponse,
        TrainingMetricsResponse,
    )

    # fmt: off
    # System
    app.get("/health")(h.health)
    # MCP
    app.get("/mcp/servers")(h.list_servers)
    app.get("/mcp/tools")(h.list_tools)
    # Knowledge
    app.post("/knowledge/search")(h.search_knowledge)
    app.get("/knowledge/skills")(h.list_skills)
    app.get("/knowledge/skills/{skill_name}")(h.get_skill)
    # Swarm
    app.post("/swarm/debate", response_model=DebateResponse)(h.run_debate)
    app.get("/swarm/perspectives")(h.get_perspectives)
    app.get("/swarm/metrics")(h.get_metrics)
    # Notebooks
    app.get("/notebooks")(h.list_notebooks)
    app.get("/notebooks/{name}")(h.get_notebook)
    # Simulations
    app.get("/simulations")(h.list_simulations)
    app.get("/simulations/{sim_id}")(h.get_simulation)
    # Journeys
    app.get("/journeys")(h.list_journeys)
    app.get("/journeys/{journey_id}")(h.get_journey)
    app.get("/journeys/{journey_id}/trajectory")(h.get_journey_trajectory)
    app.post("/journeys/demo")(h.create_demo_journey)
    app.get("/journeys/{journey_id}/visualize")(h.visualize_journey)
    app.get("/journeys/{journey_id}/plot")(h.plot_journey)
    app.get("/compare/calm-vs-llm/{journey_id}")(h.compare_calm_llm)
    # FLUME VAE
    app.post("/flume/train", response_model=FlumeTrainResponse)(h.train_flume)
    app.get("/flume/status", response_model=FlumeStatusResponse)(h.flume_status)
    app.post("/flume/encode", response_model=FlumeEncodeResponse)(h.flume_encode)
    app.post("/flume/decode", response_model=FlumeDecodeResponse)(h.flume_decode)
    app.post("/flume/interpolate", response_model=FlumeInterpolateResponse)(h.flume_interpolate)
    # Templates
    app.post("/templates/parse", response_model=TemplateParseResponse)(h.parse_template)
    # RL
    app.post("/rl/train", response_model=RLTrainResponse)(h.train_rl)
    app.get("/rl/policy/{agent_id}", response_model=RLPolicyResponse)(h.get_rl_policy)
    app.post("/rl/step", response_model=RlStepResponse)(h.rl_step)
    app.post("/rl/episode", response_model=RlEpisodeResponse)(h.rl_episode)
    app.get("/rl/policy-info", response_model=RlPolicyInfoResponse)(h.rl_policy_info)
    # Skills
    app.post("/skills/{skill_name}/execute", response_model=SkillExecuteResponse)(h.execute_skill)
    app.post("/query/find-capable-agent")(h.find_capable_agent)
    app.get("/skills/list")(h.list_prime_skills)
    # Metrics
    app.get("/metrics/agents")(h.metrics_agents)
    app.get("/metrics/training", response_model=TrainingMetricsResponse)(h.metrics_training)
    app.get("/metrics/pipeline", response_model=PipelineStatusResponse)(h.metrics_pipeline)
    app.get("/metrics/system", response_model=SystemMetricsResponse)(h.metrics_system)
    app.post("/knowledge/query", response_model=KnowledgeQueryResponse)(h.knowledge_query)
    app.get("/metrics/tokens", response_model=TokenMetricsResponse)(h.metrics_tokens)
    # Swarm execution
    app.post("/swarm/execute", response_model=SwarmExecuteResponse)(h.swarm_execute)
    # Compound engineering
    app.get("/metrics/compound", response_model=CompoundMetricsResponse)(h.metrics_compound)
    app.post("/compound/execute", response_model=CompoundExecuteResponse)(h.compound_execute)
    app.post("/compound/feedback", response_model=CompoundFeedbackResponse)(h.compound_feedback)
    app.get("/compound/health", response_model=CompoundHealthResponse)(h.compound_health)
    app.get("/compound/history/{skill_name}", response_model=CompoundHistoryResponse)(h.compound_history)
    # fmt: on


_register_routes()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn

    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8080)

content.thinking:
The `__setattr__` hook isn't working. This is because Python's module `__setattr__` doesn't work the same way as class `__setattr__`. In Python 3.7+, module `__getattr__` is supported but `__setattr__` isn't (it's not a thing for modules). When you do `api_module._vae_trainer = 'RESET'`, Python just sets it in the module's `__dict__` directly, bypassing any `__setattr__`.

So the module `__getattr__` works for reading (when the name isn't found in `__dict__`), but writing always goes to `__dict__`.


Once a value is written to the module dict, subsequent reads pull from there instead of triggering `__getattr__`. The solution is to create a custom module class that overrides `__setattr__` to intercept writes.

I'm implementing a module subclass that proxies both reads and writes for the singleton attributes through `__getattr__` and `__setattr__`, then swapping the current module's class to use this custom implementation.

Orchestrates execution lifecycle:
  1. Query vault for experience guidance (prior similar runs)
  2. Execute task with guidance
  3. Log execution trajectory, decisions, metrics to vault
  4. Extract reusable patterns for future runs
"""

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import time

    from cohezion.compound.skill_refiner import SkillRefiner
else:
    # Lazy import to avoid circular dependency at runtime
    InflectionDetector = None
    SkillRefiner = None


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_background_tasks: set[asyncio.Task[Any]] = set()


def _run_async_guardrail(coro: Any) -> Any:
    """Execute async guardrail check in sync context.

    Non-blocking on failure - logs and returns None.

    Args:
        coro: Async coroutine to execute

    Returns:
        Result of coroutine or None on failure
    """
    try:
        return asyncio.run(coro)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.debug(f"Guardrail check failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return None


@dataclass
class ExecutionResult:
    """Result of a compound execution."""

    success: bool
    output: str
    metrics: dict[str, Any]
    duration_seconds: float
    vault_experiment_path: str = ""
    vault_decision_paths: list[str] | None = None
    token_metrics: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    """Executor for compound engineering tasks with vault integration.

    Lifecycle:
      1. get_experience_guidance() - Query vault for similar tasks
      2. execute_task() - Run the task with token-efficient client
      3. Logs are persisted to vault automatically
      4. extract_patterns() - Save reusable insights

    def _compute_token_delta(
        self,
        metrics_before: dict[str, Any] | None,
        metrics_after: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Compute token metric deltas (tokens used in this execution).

        Args:
            metrics_before: Token metrics before execution
            metrics_after: Token metrics after execution

        Returns:
            Dict with token delta information
        """
        if not metrics_before:
            # First execution, can't compute delta
            return metrics_after

        delta: dict[str, Any] = {}

        # Compute differences
        if "total_tokens" in metrics_after and "total_tokens" in metrics_before:
            delta["tokens_used"] = metrics_after["total_tokens"] - metrics_before["total_tokens"]
        if "api_calls" in metrics_after and "api_calls" in metrics_before:
            delta["api_calls_made"] = metrics_after["api_calls"] - metrics_before["api_calls"]
        if "cache_hits" in metrics_after and "cache_hits" in metrics_before:
            delta["cache_hits"] = metrics_after["cache_hits"] - metrics_before["cache_hits"]
        if "cache_misses" in metrics_after and "cache_misses" in metrics_before:
            delta["cache_misses"] = metrics_after["cache_misses"] - metrics_before["cache_misses"]

        # Include final hit rate
        if "cache_hit_rate" in metrics_after:
            delta["cache_hit_rate"] = metrics_after["cache_hit_rate"]

        # Pass through model name and other non-delta fields
        if "model" in metrics_after:
            delta["model"] = metrics_after["model"]
        if "combined_hit_rate" in metrics_after:
            delta["combined_hit_rate"] = metrics_after["combined_hit_rate"]
        if "tokens_per_second" in metrics_after:
            delta["tokens_per_second"] = metrics_after["tokens_per_second"]

        return delta
